Definition: from G1537 and G3670; to acknowledge or (by implication, of assent) agree fully:--confess, profess, promise.
BiblicalUsage: exomologéō means confess, profess, promise. In Matthew 3:6, the text says "confessing their sins." In Mark 1:5, the text says "confessing their sins."
TheologicalSignificance: My position is simple: exomologéō tells me that repentance is not grovelling; it is turning around and walking the other way. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
RelatedEvents: The Baptism of Jesus; Jesus Sends Out the Seventy-Two; The Sons of Sceva at Ephesus
